title: CADder Bridge rig manifest
description: Kinematic description of a SolidWorks assembly, written by Peak.Cadder next to a STEP export. Units are metres and radians. All vectors and transforms are in the assembly's global frame (right-handed, Z-up). See SCHEMA.md for semantics.

file.description: STEP file name relative to the manifest

sha1.description: SHA-1 of the STEP file, guards against stale pairs

occurrence_matching.description: Id of the matcher that produced step_occurrence_path values

id.description: Stable per-occurrence id, unique in this manifest (c001, c002, ...)

step_name.description: Exact PRODUCT name written to the STEP file

step_occurrence_path.description: Occurrence path in the STEP tree; null when matching failed (see warnings)

id.description: g000, g001, ... g000 is conventionally the grounded group

name.description: Human slug used for the bone name; the id stays authoritative

components.description: Empty for a synthesized carrier link: a virtual body splitting a tangent contact's motion into two primitive joints. It gets a bone and owns no geometry.

bbox_diag.description: Diagonal of the group's combined bounding box, metres; bone-length heuristic

axis.description: Unit vector, global frame. Null for ball and free joints

secondary_axis.description: Unit vector not parallel to axis; fixes bone roll deterministically. Never null when axis is set. For pin_slot it is semantic: the slide direction, perpendicular to axis

driver_joint.description: Joint id whose motion drives this one; null for screw self-coupling

ratio.description: gear: rad/rad, negative = reversal. linear_coupler: m/m

samples.description: table only: the driven joint's value as a sampled function of the driver's, [[x, y], ...] with x ascending, both relative to the exported pose and in the joints' own units (radians for a turn, metres for a slide). Read off the live model: a cam profile, or a universal joint's fluctuation with the yokes' phase in it. The consumer interpolates between samples.

periodic.description: table only: the relation repeats every `period` of x (a full turn of the driver)

period.description: table only: the period of x when periodic, else 0

mirror_scope.description: mirror only: how much of the pose is mirrored. plane = a symmetric mate between planar faces, so only the translation along the normal and the two tilts follow. rigid = an assembly mirror feature, so every freedom follows. Absent means plane.

cam.description: cam only: the cam path's faces and the follower's contact entity. The consumer holds the follower on the faces live: a vertex or a roller by projection along the follower's slide, a flat face by the support function of the faces along the face normal. Written when the exporter could not table the cam (a cam free in its plane, or on a slide) or did not turn it

axis.description: The cam's joint axis, unit, global

origin.description: A point on the cam's joint axis, global metres

surface.description: The cam path's faces triangulated in global metres at the exported pose

point.description: vertex: the vertex. roller: a point on the roller's axis (or a ball follower's centre). flat: a point on the face. Global metres

axis.description: roller only: the roller's axis, unit, global

radius.description: roller only: the roller's (or ball's) radius, metres

normal.description: flat only: the face normal, unit, global

mirror_plane.description: mirror only: the plane the driven joint's body is reflected across; mirror_scope says how much of the pose follows

path.description: Path joints only: the sampled curve the child follows, ordered along the path, global metres. axis is the tangent at the rest position

surface.description: Surface joints only: the face the child's point stays on, triangulated in global metres. axis is the surface normal at the rest position

mechanisms.description: Loops that share joints, each with every input the mechanism can take as a COMPLETE alternative. A consumer that lets the user pick the input applies an option whole: it replaces the mechanism's loops with the option's and swaps parent and child on the option's flipped joints. The exporter's own choice is inputs[0], whose loops equal the top-level loops and whose flipped list is empty.

loops.description: Ids of the mechanism's loops in the top-level list

joint.description: The joint that drives the mechanism under this option

loops.description: The mechanism's loops under this input: same ids, same order, re-chosen cuts, closures and members

flipped_joints.description: Joints whose parent_group and child_group swap under this input, because the tree reaches them from the other side

joint_limits.description: Joints whose limits differ under this input, with the limits that apply then (null = unlimited). A stroke limit derived onto a slider-crank's crank belongs to the crank-driven configuration. A consumer applies these with the option and restores the joints' own limits when it leaves it.

closure_joint.description: The cut edge; the consumer re-closes it instead of parenting through it

closure_kind.description: How to re-close the cut. 'ik' is a point coincidence solved by rotating the driven chain. 'aim_pair' is a slider-crank: the bodies either side of the cut hang off their own pins and aim at each other, because no rotational solver can lengthen a slide. 'none' means the tree already carries the motion and the consumer must not solve the cut at all.

mobility.description: How many inputs this loop takes: its joints' freedom less the three a planar closure spends. A loop of mobility m must leave m-1 bones of the driven chain OUT of the solve, nearest the root, for the user to pose. Counted only for a planar loop of pins and slides; 1 everywhere else.

driver_candidates.description: Every input the exporter weighed for this loop, the chosen one first, with the cut each implies. Informative: to switch inputs a consumer applies a mechanism option, never a candidate on its own.

mat4.description: Row-major 4x4; rows are [R|t] with bottom row [0,0,0,1]; translation in metres

value_at_rest.description: The mate's dimension value in the exported (as-mated) configuration. Consumers apply min-value_at_rest .. max-value_at_rest as deltas from rest pose
